pages.heading: ARTIST STATEMENT
pages.text:
Shaped by life across California, Mississippi, and now Texas, I’m self-
taught and soul-driven. I’ve spent my life following the pull of
creativity. From an early commission at sixteen to showing in global art
capitals like Florence and Miami, I’ve trusted the process.
I paint in reverse—and not just for the fun of making people tilt their
heads. My art plays with perception. For me, art is not just visual; it's
experiential. Through backwards text and vibrant color, I invite viewers
to slow down, look again, and be fully present in that moment. My
process is intuitive, but intentional. I like to mix beauty with meaning,
and polish with play. Whether I’m painting live for a crowd or layering
paint in my studio, I’m always chasing that electric moment when a
piece clicks—when someone connects with it, even if they can’t quite
explain why.
My work lives in hundreds of private and corporate collections and has
been embraced by major institutions, including MOCA and the Whitney.
These recognitions fuel my mission to make art that captivates and
connects. Through vibrant palettes and layered meanings, I seek to
transform everyday spaces into portals of curiosity and joy. At the end
of the day, I’m just here to make the world a little more colorful, a little
more curious, and a lot more fun to look at.
– ARTIST STATEMENT

pages.heading: BIO
pages.text:
California born, Mississippi raised, and Texas based, Angela Fabbri is a
self-taught artist. Internationally recognized for her backwards text-
based work, she has earned praise from press, celebrity and
international collectors. With her contemporary realism and bold use of
color, she has achieved milestones, including exhibiting at the
prestigious 2019 Florence Biennale in Italy, a solo exhibition in the
artistic haven of Marfa, TX, and consecutive participation in the largest
art week in the world, Art Basel Week Miami.
Her creative talent manifested early on when, at the age of 16, she
received her first commission. With over 25 years creating, Fabbri has
been a professional artist since 2017, and her work can be found in 100s
of private and corporate collections.
The Museum of Contemporary Art (MOCA) in Los Angeles recognized
her talent in 2017, selecting her work for a group exhibition in Houston,
a gesture echoed again in 2018 by the assistant curator for the Whitney
in New York. Live painting events for Baccarat, Thrillist, and Dos Equis
further established her presence in an interactive way.
In 2019, Fabbri expanded her engagement with art enthusiasts by
establishing a popup gallery at Houston's luxury shopping destination,
The River Oaks District. With iconic neighbors, Harry Winston, Hermes
and others, Fabbri's kaleidoscopic world of color became a captivating
destination for three exhilarating months.
Fabbri’s work has been featured in several publications including,
Vogue, The Washington Post, The Houston Chronicle, Modern Luxury,
Paper City, The Book of Lists, and The Round Top Show Guide. She
looks forward to continuing her passionate journey in this wonderful
world of color. BIO

pages.heading: IN CONVERSATION
pages.text:
Inspiration comes to me from all places at
all times...it could be the color of a vine
growing on the side of a building, a word
someone says during a dinner conversation,
or a lyric from a song. Each body of work or
individual painting has its own specific
inspiration or story I'm trying to tell, but one
underlying theme throughout my work is
that time is our most valuable currency. We
can't work harder for more, we can't save it
up, and it doesn't compound. Some of my
paintings are bolder in conveying this, like
my clocks with the backwards message
"Invest Wisely" and some more subtle with
layers of detail that you would only see if
you stood still to enjoy the moment.
O ne of the most surprising moments I’ve had
was at my opening in Round Top Texas
during the Design Show when a viewer
complemented my work, specifically liking
that I did my words backwards so that it
forces you to slow down and be in the
moment. I was so pleasantly shocked that
she understood exactly what I was doing
and why....explaining it to me as if she were
the creator. All being the first time she had
been exposed to my work. That feeling,
knowing that the viewer "got it" organically
was so rewarding. IN CONVERSATION

pages.heading: IN CONVERSATION
pages.text:
IN CONVERSATION I conti nuously explore my techniques,
working to loosen and refine in all the right
ways. I want my work to have an effortless
but intentional feel with the different
techniques that I combine. Loose, messy
stencil paint that bleeds outside the lines
against sharp, crisp edges from an opposing
detail. Challenging myself with different
subjects, unexpected color combinations,
asking myself how I can add another layer to
the story I'm telling. Life experiences are so
transformative. They provide perspective,
great levels of joy, sadness, appreciation,
adventure, accomplishment...all stories I
want to tell through my work.
J oy, laughter, confusion, curiosity,
accomplishment, are all just some of the
feels I hope to evoke in my viewers. At first
glance, the viewer is drawn to my work
because the color or subject grabs their
attention. From there I want to spark their
curiosity with my backwards text, pulling
them in to focus a little more intently
because it's harder to read backwards...it
forces you to slow down. At that moment,
they have been on an effortless journey,
guiding them to a fully present place.

pages.heading: COMMISSIONS
pages.text:
Initial Consultation: Begin by discussing your
desired size, color palette, and the specific
space where the artwork will be displayed.
Angela encourages sharing inspiration images or
fabric swatches to ensure the piece aligns with
your environment.
Design Proposal: Angela will provide a design
concept or mock-up based on your preferences.
This stage allows for adjustments to ensure the
artwork meets your expectations.
Agreement and Deposit: Once the design is
approved, a contract is established outlining the
project's scope, timeline, and pricing. A deposit
is required to initiate the work.
Creation Process: Angela will commence the
creation of the artwork, keeping you informed
with progress updates. Your feedback is
welcomed to ensure the piece evolves
according to your vision.
Completion and Delivery: Upon completion, the
final piece is delivered to your location of
preference. COMMISSIONS
